confirmed_blocking.claim_broken: DR-3 / the rc10b docstring say rollback.sh 'gives up after READY_S with exit 4' and that the failing probe is retried ('only retries of the failing probe'). Nothing checks that a probe is retried at all. rc10's stubs answer 200 on the first call, and rc10b only asserts `retries and set(retries) == {probe}`, which a single call satisfies. This is a claimed invariant with no killable test, and a drill that passes while rollback.sh would fail on a real host where the restarted gateway is not ready on the first curl.
confirmed_blocking.evidence: Hand mutant H1 changes lib.sh wait_http `until curl -fsS -o /dev/null --max-time 5 "$1"; do` to `until curl ... "$1" || return 1; do` (one try, no retry). It SURVIVES rc10b (`2 passed, 13 deselected`), rc10 on the private D harness (`1 passed, 14 deselected in 7.07s`) and all of tests/i (`143 passed in 199.89s`). I2B's tests/i/mutants.py has no wait_http retry mutant either. Direct probe (stub: 8001/readyz fails once, then 200): with the real lib.sh, rollback.sh exits 0 after curl 8001, curl 8001, curl 8002, docker inspect, docker exec reload, so lib.sh does retry and the second 200 ends the wait. With H1 it exits 4 ('the restored runtime is not ready') after one curl. The drills cannot tell the two apart.
confirmed_blocking.minimal_fix: In rc10b, assert `len(retries) > 1`. With READY_S=1 and POLL_S=0.01 it makes about 100 calls. Better, add an rc10 variant, or give rc10 a stub, whose 8001/readyz fails once and then answers: assert exit 0, `issued.count(curl 8001) == 2`, and then the 8002 probe and the edge reload. Declare H1 as an i3bm mutant killed there.

votes.reason: Confirmed at 662c07c. lib.sh:27-33 wait_http loops `until curl ...; do [deadline] || return 1; sleep POLL_S; done`. The rc10 STUB (test_recovery.py:674-675) exits 0 unless argv matches INFRX_I3B_FAIL, so in rc10 every readiness probe answers on the first call and the retry loop never runs. The rc10b assertion `retries and set(retries) == {curl ... ready}` (line 853) is satisfied by a single call. Smallest experiment: I copied the worktree to scratch and applied H1 (`until curl ... "$1" || return 1; do`, so one try and no retry) to apps/infrx-api/deploy/lib.sh. Then I ran `pytest -k rc10b test_recovery.py`, which resolves DEPLOY through kit.ROOT = HERE.parents[3], meaning the mutated copy. Result: `2 passed, 13 deselected in 0.29s`. The unmutated original gives `2 passed in 2.06s`, so the mutant was exercised: it gives up immediately where the original waits READY_S. rc10 cannot kill H1 because its probes never fail. The only wait_http mutant in mutants_i3b.py (line 236) flips `&&` to `;` between the two probes. None targets the retry. So DR-3 and rc10b's docstring ('gives up after READY_S with exit 4') claim an invariant with no killable test, and a rollback.sh that would exit 4 on a real host whose restarted gateway is not ready at the first curl passes every drill. Under the stated rubric this is an invariant with no killable test, so it is blocking, although production lib.sh is correct today. Fix as proposed: assert `len(retries) > 1` in rc10b, or better add a fail-once stub case (exit 0, curl 8001 issued twice, then 8002 and the edge reload) and declare H1 as an i3bm mutant. I started no container, removed the scratch copy, and left the worktree clean.

I confirmed the finding at 662c07c. rc10b checks `retries and set(retries) == {probe}`, and a single curl satisfies that. rc10's stub exits 0 on its first call, so no test ever sends a second probe. I ran rc10b from a git-archive copy of HEAD in scratch, with an extra print of len(retries). With H1 applied to lib.sh wait_http (`until curl ... "$1" || return 1; do`), both cases pass (2 passed) and each makes 1 retry. With the original lib.sh, both pass with 48 and 71 retries. So a wait_http that gives up after one attempt is indistinguishable from one that polls for READY_S. rollback.sh exits 4 either way, and rc10 never exercises a probe that fails and then succeeds.

The claim this leaves untested is written down in two places: the rc10b docstring says rollback.sh "gives up after READY_S with exit 4", and the DR-3 row of the I3B-followup evidence says rc10b checks "only retries of the failing probe". The only mutants declared against DR-3 are i3bm97 (wait_ready || true) and i3bm98 (&& to ;). The I3B mutant list and tests/i/mutants.py have no mutant against wait_http's retry.

On a real host a restarted gateway that is not ready on the first curl would get exit 4 from H1, and the drill would still pass. That is an invariant the drill claims but has no test that can kill, so it counts as blocking under the stated rubric.

Minimal fix: in rc10b, assert len(retries) > 1. Add an rc10 variant whose stub fails 8001/readyz once and then answers 200, and assert exit 0, exactly two 8001 curls, then the 8002 probe and the edge reload. Declare H1 as an i3bm mutant killed by that variant.

The scratch copy is removed. I used no container, because rc10b needs no database and the survival follows from rc10's first-call-200 stub.

nonblocking.line: IR R2-B (the private = None override in run_one)
nonblocking.claim_broken: IR R2-B is meant to keep the D harness lock shared (DR-2). It shares the lock only with whatever TMPDIR the parent process has.
nonblocking.evidence: In my runner run (TMPDIR=/tmp/claude-1000/restore-tmp, R2-B applied), the children's lock landed at /tmp/claude-1000/restore-tmp/infrx-d3-postgres-55434.lock, not in the shared /tmp. For my run, R2-B changed only where the lock lives: all 4 mutants were killed, with problems null. Under the protocol's required private TMPDIR, R2-B does not coordinate with another lane that holds /tmp/infrx-d3-postgres-55434.lock. The lane's DR-2 measurement (lock held in $TMPDIR) is consistent with this, but 'the harness lock stays shared' holds only when the parent TMPDIR is the shared one.
nonblocking.minimal_fix: Document in IR R2-B that the D-mode mutant run must be started with the shared TMPDIR (or have pgharness put its lock in a fixed directory independent of TMPDIR). Alternatively, rely on the port-owner label check instead.

nonblocking.claim_broken: R2-B says it makes D-mode recovery suites keep the harness lock shared. The pgharness lock is `gettempdir()/<container>-<port>.lock`, so it is shared only among runs with the same TMPDIR. The evidence's own advice to run each list under a private TMPDIR recreates DR-2 between two concurrent list runs on d3.
nonblocking.evidence: Applied in scratch. e3bm23 and e3bm31 anchors each still occur exactly once (checked via mutants.MUTANTS before/occurrences: 1/1). For my run, R2-B changed nothing for locking, because my private task's lock is the absolute /tmp/infrx-confirm-i3bf-drill.lock. Its only effect was that the children used my run's TMPDIR instead of the per-mutant copy's tmp. The full list still gave 96/94/1/1.
nonblocking.minimal_fix: Keep R2-B. Put the D-mode lock at a TMPDIR-independent path (for example /tmp or /run/lock), or have R2-C/the runner document that D-mode list runs must share one TMPDIR.
